content: The QTc interval is prolonged by both moxifloxacin and venlafaxine. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended when these drugs are co-administered. Therapy modification may be necessary. Moxifloxacin enhances the effects of vildagliptin through pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution and monitoring are advised. Quinolone antibiotics, including moxifloxacin, can cause dysglycemia, manifesting as either hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia. Gatifloxacin is most likely to cause dysglycemia, while moxifloxacin is least likely. Moxifloxacin and voclosporin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Moxifloxacin and voriconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Moxifloxacin increases the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Zinc reduces the absorption and effectiveness of moxifloxacin by forming complexes in the gastrointestinal tract. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Oral moxifloxacin should be administered 4 hours before or 8 hours after products containing polyvalent cations. Moxifloxacin increases the levels of alprazolam by inhibiting its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Moxifloxacin reduces the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. Moxifloxacin reduces the levels or effects of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. Moxifloxacin increases the levels of chlordiazepoxide, clonazepam, clorazepate, estazolam, flurazepam, loprazolam, lorazepam, lormetazepam, midazolam, oxazepam, quazepam, temazepam, and triazolam by inhibiting their metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Moxifloxacin, when combined with foscarnet, may increase the risk of tonic-clonic seizures. The mechanism of this interaction is unknown, and the clinical significance is unclear. Moxifloxacin and isotretinoin may increase the risk of phototoxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Itraconazole and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Moxifloxacin reduces the levels or effects of pantothenic acid, pyridoxine, and thiamine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. Quercetin reduces the effects of moxifloxacin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Moxifloxacin increases the toxicity of amifampridine, likely by lowering the seizure threshold. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Moxifloxacin increases the toxicity of aminolevulinic acid (oral and topical) through pharmacodynamic synergy, enhancing phototoxic reactions. Alternative drugs should be considered. Moxifloxacin and amiodarone both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Moxifloxacin and amisulpride both prolong the QTc interval. ECG monitoring is recommended if co-administration is unavoidable. Moxifloxacin and amitriptyline both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Moxifloxacin and amoxapine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Moxifloxacin and anagrelide both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Moxifloxacin and apomorphine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Moxifloxacin and arformoterol both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Moxifloxacin and aripiprazole both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Moxifloxacin and arsenic trioxide both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Moxifloxacin and artemether both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Moxifloxacin and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Moxifloxacin and asenapine (oral and transdermal) both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Moxifloxacin and azithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Moxifloxacin reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. Moxifloxacin and corticosteroids (e.g., betamethasone, cortisone, dexamethasone) may increase the risk of tendon rupture. Caution and monitoring are advised. Moxifloxacin and dichlorphenamide both reduce serum potassium levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. Moxifloxacin and diclofenac may increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Moxifloxacin and didanosine reduce each other's levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Moxifloxacin and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Moxifloxacin and clomipramine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Moxifloxacin and clozapine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Moxifloxacin and crizotinib both prolong the QTc interval. ECG monitoring is recommended, along with caution and monitoring. Moxifloxacin and dasatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Moxifloxacin and degarelix both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Moxifloxacin and desflurane both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Moxifloxacin and desipramine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Moxifloxacin and deuterabenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Certain conditions, such as bradycardia, hypokalemia, or hypomagnesemia, may increase the risk of torsades de pointes and sudden death. Moxifloxacin and chloroquine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Moxifloxacin and ceritinib both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Moxifloxacin and cholera vaccine exhibit pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration should be avoided, as systemic antibiotics may inactivate the vaccine strain. Cholera vaccine should not be administered to patients who have received antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. Moxifloxacin and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously in combination with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. Moxifloxacin and citalopram both prolong the QTc interval. ECG monitoring is recommended, along with caution and monitoring. Moxifloxacin and calcium salts (e.g., calcium acetate, calcium carbonate, calcium chloride, calcium citrate, calcium gluconate) reduce each other's levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised, and administration should be separated by 2 hours. Moxifloxacin and carbonyl iron reduce each other's levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used.
